title: The Skarl Tally-Board
author: the Skarl clan's delvers, and one other hand
body:
# The Skarl Tally-Board

*Burned into a board of larch nailed beside the adit, the clan's marks in rows.*

---

Six hands at the face. Tin, two baskets. — Six hands. Tin, three baskets. — Six hands. Water in the low gallery. — Five hands; Rudd's foot. Tin, one basket. — Six hands. The big vein, the big vein, the big vein.

*The rows stop. Under them, burned deeper than the rest, the clan's sign for a debt owed and not yet paid, and a boy's name in Valish letters the clan's burner did not know how to make, so that the C of Colley is backwards.*

*Across all of it, cut with a knife and not burned, one woodfolk notch. Under the notch, more notches, one for every month since. The newest is fresh.*

title: Corra Bracken's Count
author: Corra Bracken, hunter of the Hollow
body:
# Corra Bracken's Count

*Scratched on a strip of birch bark and wedged into the tally-post's split.*

---

For whoever reads the post, since reading is what it is for now.

A notch is a hart. A long notch is a hart with twelve tines or more. A notch with a cross over it is a hind, which even a poacher should be ashamed of.

The heads go east to the Pale in the morning and the crates go west to the Wold Water in the evening. I do not follow them. It is not custom to follow them. I sit in my oak and I cut the post, which is not custom either, but nobody has told me so.

Two hundred and eleven. The post is full again. I have started on the oak.

title: The Listeners' Log, the Last Leaf
author: Sayer Imber Vane of the Circle, Listener
body:
# The Listeners' Log, the Last Leaf

*One leaf of a Sayers' log, weighted under the middle horn's tripod with a brass plumb.*

---

Thirtieth night. Wind west, light. The Moot's note carries to the camp after the second hour, very faint, and under it on the east horn the sound we have been hearing since the tenth night, which Ansa calls the tide and I call footsteps and the dog calls nothing at all but will not lie down while it lasts.

It is not the Briar moving. We have listened to the Briar. The Briar creaks like a ship.

It is somebody walking north along the far side of the thorn, at a walker's pace, every night, and it has come level with the northern gate on each of the last three nights and stopped.

Tomorrow we go through and ask them. Whoever finds this: the horns are the Circle's and should go back to the Spire. We will not need them. We will be able to hear it plainly from there.

title: How the Thorn Is Laid
author: the thorn-layers of the Layers' Ring
body:
# How the Thorn Is Laid

*Cut into the lintel stone over the ring's gap, and gone over in charcoal so it can be read.*

---

Gauntlets to the elbow. Hook in the right, the left for the pin.

Take the runner that is already there. Never cut it. Bend it down and pin it into the thorn beside it with a crook of hazel, and it roots where it touches.

Where there is nothing to bend, plant from the Nursery, three cuttings to a yard, leaning in.

Do not lay thorn anywhere the thorn has not been. We lay the Briar. We did not grow it, and we do not know what it is for, and a layer who thinks she knows is a layer who will lay it in the wrong place.

Sleep inside the ring. The thorn does not like to be slept beside.

title: On Unstringing
author: Aud Yewman, bowyer of Stave Hollow
body:
# On Unstringing

*Written on the back of a bowyer's order, nailed inside the house door.*

---

A bow is strung by the one who will draw it and unstrung by the one who made it. That is the whole of the custom and I did not write it; I only keep it.

You slip the loop off the upper nock and let the stave come straight. It takes no strength. The stave has been bent for twenty years or forty and it straightens in your hands all at once, like somebody letting out a breath they did not know they were holding. Then you carry it up the tor.

Forty years I have made them and thirty I have unstrung them, and people ask me which is harder and I tell them the second, and they think I mean my heart. I mean my hands. You can feel exactly how much the bow was used.

title: The Beacon Rule
author: the watchers of the Firewatch
body:
# The Beacon Rule

*Burned into a slat of oak nailed to the fire-basket's pole.*

---

Light for fire in the Wold. For nothing else.

Not for war: the Wold has none. Not for the clans: they have their own. Not for a lost child: shout. Not for a death: a death is not an emergency, however it feels.

When it is lit every forester who sees it comes with a spade and a wet sack, and comes to the smoke, not to the beacon.

Lay it again the same day. A beacon unlaid is a promise broken.

*Under it, in a newer knife:* The Firewatch is down. Who lights it now? *And under that, newer:* I do.

title: A Moss for Davy
author: Orla Colley, burner
body:
# A Moss for Davy

*Pressed flat inside a folded charcoal sack by the door of Colley's Hearth.*

---

Star-moss for his eyes because he never missed anything.
Hair-moss for his head because it never lay flat.
Feather-moss for his hands because he whittled.
Cushion-moss for his feet, because he was always tired at the end of the path, and never said.

That is his moss. I have kept it by the door eleven years with nothing under it. The Hollow's Keeper of Knots says a moss with nothing under it is a moss for nobody, and a name nobody tends goes quiet. So I tend it.

The clan's man leaves silver on the bridge every month. I have not been to the bridge. Tell him I do not want the silver. Tell him I want the boy.

title: The Measure of the Runner
author: the keepers of Rookhold
body:
# The Measure of the Runner

*Knotted cords tied to a stake at the Stray Thorn's tip, a tag of bark on each.*

---

1019: the runner crosses the wardstone. A span past it.
1024: four yards.
1030: ten yards. Edda says leave it.
1036: nineteen yards. It has flowered, which the Briar does not do.
1041: thirty-one yards.
1042: forty-two yards. Eleven in a year.

The Briar grows east, away from us, and has for nine hundred years, and the Wardstone Line is the proof. This one runner grows west.

Edda says a thing that walks away from something for nine hundred years may send one back to see if it is still there.

title: The First Tines
author: the Hart-Knights of the Tine Barrow
body:
# The First Tines

*Carved in rows on the forecourt stones of the Tine Barrow, and chalked over fresh.*

---

Here lie the knights who kept the Wold before the Wold was kept.

Ardo, who would not kill the white hart, and wore its antlers when it died old.
Bell of the Long Spear, who would not kill the hart of the Hollow ford.
Tamsen, who would not kill the hart that gored her, and wore its antlers after.
Harrow, who would not kill the hart that led him out of the Briar.

*And on, forty names. At the end, in chalk, newer:*

We do not kill harts. We never did. We wear the antlers of harts that died old, so that they are remembered, which is the only thing any of us is for. Whoever sold the antlers in Tollmere cut them off dead animals they had killed themselves, and put our name on them. — K. H.

title: Countwatch Chalk
author: Fernhold's foresters
body:
# Countwatch Chalk

*A page of the morning count, copied off the tower wall onto a forester's slate and left on the stair.*

---

Midwinter: fourteen.
Thaw: fifteen. The new one at the Moot end, the size of a cart.
Seedtime: seventeen.
Midsummer: nineteen.
This morning: eighteen.

Eighteen is not good news. The patch at the Old Gate end did not heal. It is not there. It is somewhere else.

The chalk is a stub. Alder says bring more. Alder says a lot of things to people who climb the tower at dawn.

title: The Hanging Words
author: the Woodfolk
body:
# The Hanging Words

*Scratched inside the lid of a bowyer's box at the foot of Hollin Tor.*

---

When the bow is hung, whoever carried it says:

You took what you needed.
You checked what you set.
The string is off. The arrow is home.

and nothing else, because the Woodfolk say nothing else.

*Under it, in a different hand:* The bows are never restrung. That is the point of hanging them. A bow on the tor has been let go the way the moss is let go at a grave, once nobody is left to tend it. *And under that:* Somebody has restrung one. Whoever it was, that is not letting go.

title: The Northern Keepers' Rule
author: the keepers of the northern gate
body:
# The Northern Keepers' Rule

*Cut into a flat stone at the foot of Harrow Tor's cairn, half under moss.*

---

Walk the road at first light.
Lift every stone that fell in the night.
Carry it up the tor. Do not throw it in the bracken; the bracken does not want it either.
A clear road is a promise that someone will come down it.

*The rule ends there. Somebody has cleared the moss off it recently, and the road below is clear, and there is no one on the tor.*

title: What the Grey Man Hears
author: a Fernhold forester
body:
# What the Grey Man Hears

*Pencilled on the back of a Fernhold count-sheet and tucked into a crack in the middle brother.*

---

Climbed the Grey Man at dusk on a still day to see if what they say is so.

It is. From the top you can hear the Moot, though it is miles off: a hum like a hive in a wall.

They say it has a word in it. I sat an hour and I will write down what I heard and you may laugh.

It is not a word. It is a name. It is said the way you say a name when you are calling somebody in for supper and you do not expect them to answer the first time.

I did not know the name. I have not slept well.

title: The Chapel's Count
author: the knight who keeps the Antler Chapel
body:
# The Chapel's Count

*Chalked on a board propped against the chapel's broken altar.*

---

Antlers hung in this chapel, each from a hart that died old: three hundred and six.
Antlers missing since the poachers came to the Wold: forty.
Antlers seen in Tollmere, in the windows of the Lantern Row, sold as Oroth relics: I have not been to Tollmere. I am told a great many.

I ask whoever reads this for the forty back. I do not ask for the rest. The rest were never ours.

title: Out of the Mere, Dry
author: Nessa Ashby, of Ormhold
body:
# Out of the Mere, Dry

*A letter folded small and pushed into a crack in the rock beside the top fall.*

---

Tam, you will want this written down so that the Hollow believes it.

Hobb Ashby's girl went into the top fall of Blackgill on the eve of the thaw, reaching for a torch that had not caught. We searched the gill all night. On the second morning a Gullhithe eel-wife pulled her out of the Mere by her collar, three days' walk off, and she was dry. Dry to her boots. Not a weed on her.

She says it was dark and warm and a long way, and that the water under the Wold goes somewhere before it comes out, and that there were lights in it.

Do not tell her mother I have written this. Tell the Circle, if you like; they will not believe it either.

title: Measuring the Hart
author: Sayer Ottilie Crane of the Circle
body:
# Measuring the Hart

*A page of a Sayer's notebook, weighted under a knuckle of the skull.*

---

Skull, nose to nape: nine paces and a half. Antler span, tine to tine: twenty-two paces. Tines counted on the left: sixty-one. On the right: fifty-nine, two broken.

No beast of that size is in any record the Circle keeps, the Oroth's included.

The clans say it is a giant's dog. The Hart-Knights say it is the Hart, and will not say which hart. I say it is a mistake in the record, which is to say something the record has lost the name of, which is to say it is exactly the kind of thing the Circle exists to find.

The knight at the skull has asked me to stop measuring it. I have one more tine to count.

title: A Poacher's Reckoning
author: one of the Hunters' Stand
body:
# A Poacher's Reckoning

*A greasy page folded into a knot-hole of the hide's floor.*

---

Harts this season: 14. Hinds: don't count them.
Paid at the Pale: 2 the tine. 14 heads, 9 tines a head near enough: 252.
Less the Pale's cut for the salt and the crates: 60.
Less arrows, gut, the ladder rope: 11.
Owed to Jory from last winter: 30.

The factor says Tollmere sells them at forty the tine.

Forty. The tine.

Somebody is a thief here and it is not me.

title: The Clamps' Day-Book
author: Sorrel and Barnaby Rooke
body:
# The Clamps' Day-Book

*A day-book left open on a cordwood stack, in two hands that alternate line by line.*

---

S: wind from the east. — B: is it. — S: second clamp fretful. — B: turned it. — S: sold four sacks to the Hollow. — B: tallyman's clerk came asking for the Pale road. Sent him the long way. — S: good. — B: two carriers with antler crates at dusk, going west, wet sacking over. — S: saw them. — B: said nothing. — S: custom. — B: mistake. — S: is it.

title: The Verderer's Fires
author: the verderer of the High Wold
body:
# The Verderer's Fires

*Chalked on the underside of the tower's top deck, where it can only be read lying down.*

---

Fires seen in the Wold this year: 3 (burners; one lightning).
Fires seen in the Wold ten years back: 9.
Twenty years back: 17.

Fires seen past the Thornmarch, where there is nothing, ever: 1.

I have been watching it since the first night. It does not move. It is not getting bigger. Every night, a little after the Moot's hum starts, somebody walks away from it with a light, north along the thorn, and it goes out, and in the morning it is there again.

I am not coming down until I know who is tending it. Wat can bring the bread up.

title: Marks in the Face
author: a Tollmere mason
body:
# Marks in the Face

*A rubbing on waxed linen, pinned to the quarry face with a mason's nail.*

---

Rubbed from the cut face, where the Builders' masons left their marks on every block before they lifted it: a square, a square with a tail, a hand, a hand with two tails.

The same marks are on the Long Stride's kerbs in Tollmere, under the paint the Charter put on them.

The Guild's history says the Stride's stone was brought by the Builders from nowhere anybody knows. It was brought from here, from a wood the Guild calls savage, by masons who signed their work.

I have been asked not to publish this. I am pinning it to the rock instead, where the rock can publish it.

title: Three Days Kneeling
author: Wystan Tine, Hart-Knight
body:
# Three Days Kneeling

*Scratched on a slate set against the Moot Gate Stone's foot, facing the gate.*

---

I kneel here because the first knights knelt here, facing the gate the Hart came through, before they took the antlers.

I have taken the antlers. I did it twenty years ago. I am kneeling again because I want to know whether it is still the same gate, and a gate is known by what comes through it, and nothing has.

If you are reading this and you are the one I am waiting for, you are late.

If you are not, do not speak to me. It is the third day and I have almost heard it.

title: What the Skarl Owe
author: Brokk ko-Skarl
body:
# What the Skarl Owe

*A page of clan tally-paper folded into a crack behind the loose stones.*

---

The clan says a death is a debt and a debt is paid. The clan went home. The debt did not.

Tosk pays silver at the middle of the bridge every month because it is the only place he can stand in both countries at once. Nobody takes it. The woodfolk say nothing. The silver lies there until the rain takes it into the Skarl Water.

I stayed. I am the one who told the lads to heap the spoil on the slope. So I am here, in the dark with the silk, and the clan has put me out of the Rope-Song for it, and I have not argued.

The boy is under the bottom gallery where the shaft drowned. I have heard his whistle. It is not him. It is the old spinner in the shaft with his whistle in her web, and when the draught comes up it plays.

title: The Builders' Hand
author: the Horn Pale's boiling-shed
body:
# The Builders' Hand

*A pattern of burnt marks on a board, pinned over the boiling vats with a skinning knife.*

---

Burn the mark on the base of the tine, where it meets the burr, after the bleaching and before the seal.

A square. A square with a tail. A hand. A hand with two tails.

Not too deep. The buyers in the Lantern Row put their thumb on it, and a mark that is too deep feels new.

*Under it, in a boiler's hand, scratched with the knife:* These are the masons' marks out of the Old Quarry. They are not the Builders' hand. They are the hand of the men who cut the stone. We are putting a mason's name on a hart.

title: The Pale's Rules
author: Wendel Crale, factor
body:
# The Pale's Rules

*Nailed to the inside of the gate, at the height of a man's eyes, so it is read on the way out.*

---

1. Heads at the gate before noon. Not after. The boilers go home.
2. Two marks the tine, paid on the tally. Hinds not bought.
3. Poachers to sleep in the yard. ALL poachers. Every night. No exceptions for weather.
4. No fires outside the pale.
5. Say nothing to the Woodfolk. They will say nothing to you. That is how this works.
6. The Hart-Knights are not to be answered, whatever they ask.

*Scratched under rule 3, small:* why

title: Grey Inside the Wold
author: a forester of Fernhold
body:
# Grey Inside the Wold

*A forester's chalk-slate propped against the nearest grey sallow, facing out.*

---

Came to cut withies. The ring is grey. All of it: leaf, bark, the moss under it, the bracken to the ring's edge, a beetle on the bark.

Nothing is dead. I cut a stem and it did not bleed and it did not snap.

Countwatch's patches are all on the thorn. This is half a mile inside. It is not on the count. Somebody should put it on the count. Somebody should tell Kit at the Ring.

I have not touched anything else. I have left the stem I cut where it fell. I did not want to carry it.

title: The Boilers' Account Book
author: the antler-boilers
body:
# The Boilers' Account Book

*A calf-bound account book with the Horn Pale's mark stamped on the cover.*

---

Received of the Hunters' Stand, heads: 14. Tines: 126. Paid at two the tine.
Sawn, boiled, bleached, sealed: 126.
Crated for the Wold Water: 11 crates.
Seal of the Pale on each. Mark of the Builders' hand burned in each tine as instructed.

Sale in Tollmere per the Ledger of Prices: forty the tine.

*In the margin, in the boilers' own hand:* Two. We get two. Of the two we pay for the salt.

title: The Factor's Price Book
author: Wendel Crale, factor for the Tallymen at the Horn Pale
body:
# The Factor's Price Book

*A Tallymen's price book in a brass-cornered case.*

---

Oroth antler, sealed: bought at the Pale at 2 the tine; sold at the Lantern Row at 40 the tine. Carriage and seal: 3. Margin to the House: 35 the tine.

Mark of the Builders' hand to be burned on the base of each tine before sealing; see the pattern pinned in the boiling-shed.

The Woodfolk will not act. Their custom forbids burning a poachers' camp while poachers are in it, and says nothing about a buyer. Keep poachers in the yard at all times.

The Hart-Knights may object. The Hart-Knights have no standing in the Charter.
